To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

LL-37 is taken up by A549 epithelial lung cells via endocytic pathways and trafficked to the perinucleus via microtubules and that A549 cells have two receptors that bind LL-37, one of which binds with high affinity.
LL-37 is taken up into lung epithelial cells and that this uptake is mediated by endocytosis.
LL-37 is taken up by epithelial cells in an energy- and receptor-dependent manner and that it traffics to the perinucleus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the interaction of LL-38 with epithelial cells.
understanding the role of LL-37 in the immune system.
the interaction of LL- 37, a cationic host-defense peptide, with lung epithelial cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LL-37 binds to two different receptors on A549 cells, and the uptake process requires endocytic elements but does not require actin.
LL-37 is taken up by A549 cells via a process dependent on endocytosis, with subsequent trafficking to the pericentriolar region of the cell.
LL-37 binds to the cell surface of A549 epithelial lung cells and is internalized into the cell by a mechanism dependent on microtubes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the human antimicrobial peptide LL-37 is internalized by A549 cells, and the internalization is dependent on actin, microtubules, and clathrin.
LL-37, a host defense peptide, is internalized by A549 epithelial cell and is localized to the perikaryon.
LL-37 interacts with epithelial cells by a receptor-mediated endocytosis process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
human LL-37 binds to A549 epithelial lung cells with high and low affinities.
LL-37 interacts with epithelial cells in a specific manner and has a potential for modulating epithelial cell function.
LL-37 interacts with epithelial cells in a receptor-mediated manner and that this process requires elements involved in endocytic uptake.
